sections.title: Giving Instructions
sections.content: To tell one person to do something, use the form you already know for él and ella. That is the whole rule: 'Carlos corta los tomates' is he cuts them, and 'Carlos, corta los tomates' is cut them. Nothing new to learn — the same word, with a name and a comma in front of it.

items.spanish: Primero calienta las tortillas, luego mezcla los ingredientes.
items.english: First heat the tortillas, then mix the ingredients.

items.spanish: Mientras cocinan, todos hablan en español.
items.english: While they cook, everyone speaks Spanish.

sections.content: Because the instruction and the he/she form are the same word, Spanish leans on the comma and the voice: 'Kaylee ralla el queso' reports what she is doing, 'Kaylee, ralla el queso' asks her to.
